Only E000 exists: the template demo (3 SGD steps on 64 images) scores acc 0.012 at 0.14 s. It is infeasible, and nothing about real recipes has been measured yet. My priors follow, organised by where the time budget goes.

1) Time = fixed cost + epochs × per-epoch cost.
- Fixed cost includes the uint8→GPU transfer (about 150 MB, roughly 0.05 s), normalisation, a whitening eigendecomposition on patches (about 0.05–0.2 s) and any compile or autotune that leaks into timed code. If build warms up correctly, the fixed cost should be well under 0.5 s, i.e. under 5–10% of an ~8–10 s run. So H3 and H3.2 are probably small levers, unless an unwarmed shape triggers max-autotune recompiles inside train. That would cost seconds, so it is a cliff, not a slope.
- Per-epoch cost: an airbench96-like net at widths 128/384/576 does roughly 3–4× the FLOPs of airbench94. My reference is airbench96 on an A100, about 1 s/epoch with compile. In eager mode with fp16 and channels_last, add about 15–30% for launches and Python overhead under the 4-CPU pin. That gives a 9-epoch eager port of about 10–12 s; compile plus a fused optimizer should bring it to about 8.5–9.5 s.

2) Accuracy at a fixed epoch count. CIFAR-100 at 75% with no TTA is demanding for 9 epochs. airbench96-style nets gain about 1 pp from TTA on CIFAR-10, and losing it hurts more on CIFAR-100. I put the 9-epoch port's mean at about 0.74–0.76, with an ~25% chance of a bug in a first port (whitening scale, lr scaling, BN momentum) dropping it far lower. Each extra epoch near 9 is worth about 0.4–0.8 pp and costs about 11% of the time. That makes epochs the main dial, and margin is bought with time.

3) Other levers trade accuracy for time with net losses:
- Progressive resizing at 24/28/32 px saves about 15–20% of compute but likely costs 0.5–1 pp at short schedules. That deficit then needs about 1 extra epoch to recover, so the net gain is small or negative.
- Muon helps sample efficiency on CIFAR-10, but its Newton-Schulz overhead on 576-wide 3×3 filters is non-trivial. The lr and batch values were tuned for airbench94/CIFAR-10, so the transfer is uncertain.
- EMA/Lookahead: small gain (0–0.3 pp) at about 1% cost.

4) Noise: I expect per-seed accuracy std of about 0.2–0.35 pp, so the 3-seed mean has an SE of about 0.15–0.2 pp. I expect run-to-run time drift of 1–2%. A 3-seed mean of about 0.756 or more is needed for safety over 40 seeds.

Unsure about:
- the absolute epochs-to-75% for this port without TTA (it could be 10–12);
- whether eager per-epoch cost is CPU-bound under the 4-core pin;
- whether the ideas listed after I001 are run with the port already in place. I assume they are.

forecasts.reason: Eager 9 epochs of a 576-wide net likely takes over 9.5 s, and accuracy without TTA is borderline at the 0.753 bar.
Likely the 9→10 branch: about +11% time and +0.5 pp, which does not test the 8.5→9 slope stated in H4.2.1.
Compile plus a fused optimizer should remove about 15–25% of eager overhead under the 4-CPU pin without changing the math.
The expected EMA gain of about 0.1–0.3 pp is comparable to the 3-seed SE.
A GPU-resident, deterministic pipeline should give under 2% time drift and per-seed std of about 0.2–0.35 pp.
The ragged batch is already warmed in I003, so dropping it saves less than 0.3 s (about 2% of steps).
Untuned hyperparameter transfer from CIFAR-10, a doubled batch (half the steps) and Newton-Schulz overhead probably offset the sample-efficiency gain.
About 15% time saved, but likely a loss of more than 0.2 pp accuracy at 9 epochs on CIFAR-100.

cruxes: What 3-seed mean accuracy does the 9-epoch port reach without TTA? This decides whether the run needs 9, 10 or 12 epochs, which is the biggest time multiplier.
Is the eager per-epoch cost CPU/launch-bound under the 4-core pin (compile saves 25% or more) or GPU-FLOP-bound (compile saves about 10%)?
Does any compile or autotune leak into timed code or eval (unwarmed shapes)? That would be a multi-second cliff rather than a small fixed cost.
